rubric.exceeds: Every claim, calculation, artifact, or performance choice is accurate and faithful to the stated criteria, with no notable errors.
rubric.meets: The work is accurate and faithful to the stated criteria, with at most one minor, self-correctable error.
rubric.developing: The work is mostly accurate but has one or more errors that affect the result or the intended effect.
rubric.beginning: The work has multiple accuracy or fidelity errors that prevent it from meeting the stated criteria.

rubric.exceeds: Every choice is backed by specific, cited evidence or clearly explained reasoning that a reader/viewer/listener can follow without help.
rubric.meets: Most choices are backed by evidence or reasoning, with only small gaps.
rubric.developing: Some choices are backed by evidence or reasoning, but several are asserted without support.
rubric.beginning: Choices are asserted with little or no supporting evidence or reasoning.

rubric.exceeds: The finished task, program, or piece fully meets the performance task as written and demonstrates independent transfer to a new example.
rubric.meets: The finished task, program, or piece meets the performance task as written.
rubric.developing: The finished task, program, or piece partially meets the performance task, with a named gap.
rubric.beginning: The finished task, program, or piece does not yet meet the performance task as written.

rubric.exceeds: There is clear evidence of testing, critique, or self-checking that produced a real, documented revision improving the work.
rubric.meets: There is evidence of at least one checking or revision step.
rubric.developing: There is little evidence of checking or revision beyond a first attempt.
rubric.beginning: There is no evidence the work was checked or revised at all.

prompts.prompt: Explain requirements and data inventory in your own words and give or identify a valid example.
Use a diagram, model, score, data display, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of structure and query implementation.
Apply validation and error handling in a new realistic situation. Show the process or cite the evidence.
Analyse a plausible error, weak claim, unsafe choice, rights problem, or design flaw involving threat model and mitigations; correct it and explain why.
Explain how privacy impact and minimization and documentation and review relate — how one supports, constrains, contrasts with, or builds on the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Deliver a secure data application with schema, tests, a threat model, mitigations, and a privacy impact review.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy or quality, and one next question.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence and reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

scoring_judgment_guidance: Score with the rubric below, not a single fixed answer key — a technical project legitimately has more than one valid solution. Compare the submission against each rubric dimension using the "performance evidence" prompt in the linked assessment record for Secure Data Project and Threat-Model Review, and record which level the student reached for each dimension along with one specific reason drawn from the actual submission.
remediation_plan: If the project stalls, step back to the smallest version of the task: rebuild just the part covering requirements and data inventory in isolation, using a worked example from this unit as a model, then re-attach it to the full project once that smaller piece works and you can explain why.
extension_plan: Once the core project is working, extend it to handle a new constraint or edge case related to structure and query implementation, or compare two different approaches to the same problem and explain the real tradeoff between them in your own words.
accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.

safety_and_privacy.note: No real credentials, live external systems, or real personal data are used anywhere in this unit's materials.
